doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Advice, listening and the record business
title: Recent recordings still require a producer
summary: With Sweet and Lovely and Honey, he again had to accept someone overseeing him in the studio.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: How do you feel about the recent things that have come out? I know you just made
some comments about Honey. I know Sweet and Lovely -­
-- is out now for a little while.
Is it different now than it was when you -- at an earlier time the recordings that you've been doing recently?
Are -- are they different in what way?
No, I mean, is it different now working with companies -­
-- with the company that you're working for?

The same because it's the recent recording that I'm talking of where I had to have a producer because they want to know what's going on in the studio. Why couldn't they let me go in? And that's another thing that pisses me, off, I mean, I'm not honest enough? They don't believe in my honesty enough where I can't go in the studio and do what I wanna do and then give them the finished product? You see, you have to have someone to oversee me? You know. That -- that -- that's a drag, too. An -- an insult, really.
